messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want a fair financial share of the house. I haven’t agreed to A buying it at a discount, and I don’t want that discount to come out of my share. This is my inheritance too. I’d like us to settle it fairly, but there’s no need to rush.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband, ideally at a family discount. Having a home we can afford would give us more independence. I know C hasn’t agreed, so I can’t proceed without her agreement.

I’d like the house and will to leave me with some money to start a dance studio. That’s important to me because it’s the way I’m hoping to build my work. I’m not sure what amount or arrangement would be fair yet.
Yes, that fits. I want my fair share, and I don’t want to be rushed.
Entry 3 fits, though I’d add that I want to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. Entry 4 isn’t quite right: I need C’s agreement to proceed with the purchase.
Yes, that wording fits. I don’t think there’s anything else to add just now.
Yes, entry 4 fits. The discount would make buying the house more affordable and help me and my husband become financially independent.

E makes sense as a first step. I’m not agreeing to a discount now; b or a seem clearest for protecting my share. I’d consider c only once the valuation and numbers are clear and the discount truly comes from A’s share. I’m uncomfortable relying on payments over time under d. My concern is making sure I’m not taking on risk or subsidizing the purchase.

E seems like a sensible first step. A discount could help make the purchase affordable, but I can’t say whether c or d would work without the figures and terms. My concern is that full market value may be beyond what we can afford. I don’t have another discomfort to add right now.

An independent valuation first, then deciding at a pace everyone’s comfortable with, sounds sensible. A full-value buyout might meet my concern if my share leaves me enough to start the studio, but I don’t know what amount that would be yet. I don’t have a smaller discomfort to add right now.
Yes, that fits. I don’t want to carry financial risk or subsidize the purchase from my share.
A mild concern: option b may be unaffordable for us at full market value. I’d need the valuation and figures before knowing whether any option could work.
A small concern is that “enough for the studio” is still vague, though I don’t know the amount yet. Please keep that as an open question rather than assume my share will cover it.
